greeting: Hello. I’m Verse, the FandomVerse guide. Ask me about any of the seven worlds, or pick a question below.
fallback: I don’t have an answer scripted for that one. Try asking about a category, bookmarks, the cart, or search — or use the quick questions below.

rules.a: FandomVerse covers seven worlds: Anime, Gaming, Movies, TV Shows, K-Pop, Comics and Manga. Each hub has its own articles, characters, galleries, media, events and merchandise. Pick one from the top navigation.

Tap the bookmark control on any card to save it. Bookmarks persist in your browser’s local storage. You can attach a personal note — notes last for the current session only — and export the whole list as formatted text.
The Trailers page aggregates every trailer, interview, podcast and community video across all seven categories. You can filter by category and by release status.
The merchandise showcase is a demonstration. You can browse items, open details and add them to a cart that totals up properly — but there is no checkout or payment, by design.
Press ⌘K (or Ctrl+K) anywhere to open search. You can also use the Search page to filter by category and content type, and sort alphabetically, by newest or by popularity.
The Events page lists conventions, screenings, watch parties and launches across every category, split into upcoming and past.
Every category has at least five character profiles with a biography, the series they appear in, and their defining traits. Open any hub and choose the Characters tab.
Each hub has an image gallery with a lightbox view, so you can browse without leaving the page. Open a hub and choose the Gallery tab.
FandomVerse is a student project built for the Web Innovation Unleashed brief. The About page covers the team, the stack and the design decisions.
The Contact page has the team’s details, a message form and a map showing where we are based.
Everything here is invented for this project — every series, character, event and product. No real franchise or artwork is used, which keeps the site fully within the brief’s original-content rule.
Login and Sign-up are interface demonstrations only. There is no backend and no account is created — nothing you type is stored or sent anywhere.
